title: Windowed selection and continuation token contract for rerank endpoint
creator: Sofia Martinez
summary: Define an ergonomic, scalable API contract for returning reranking results incrementally: explicit selection window semantics, opaque continuation token format, and deterministic per-item provenance in structured output.
description:
Why: teams using the rerank endpoint want predictable, low-latency slices of ranked results for UI rendering and batch pipelines. Current ambiguity around 'top_k' semantics, unstable reorderings when using continuation tokens, and inconsistent provenance fields cause client-side complexity and hidden cost/latency regressions.

What: establish a new contract (v2) for rerank that introduces two concepts: a selection_window (offset + limit) that is independent of internal scoring truncation, and an opaque continuation_token used only to resume the server-side rank stream for subsequent windows. Output will be structured to include per-item normalized_score, raw_score, and a provenance array. The contract emphasizes deterministic ordering, tie-handling rules, and clear latency/compute tradeoffs for partial responses.

Non-goals: changing the ranking model itself, supporting arbitrary server-side re-ranking policies per-tenant in this ticket (those are follow-ups).
technical_notes: selection_window: request fields (offset: integer >= 0, limit: integer > 0, allow_partial: boolean) where offset/limit describe the client-visible slice; server may return fewer items when downstream scoring truncated for latency/p100SLO.
continuation_token: opaque base64 blob containing (shard_id, rank_cursor_position, scoring_seed, version) signed by server; clients must treat as opaque and only send back to same endpoint/region.

ordering contract: results must be strictly deterministic for a given model version + input set + scoring_seed. Ties are broken by stable document id then by original input order to preserve UX stability.
scores: response includes normalized_score (0..1, float) for UI, raw_score (float) for debug/monitoring, and provenance: list of short tags (e.g. ["embedding_cosine","bm25_boost"]).

streaming: support chunked response where selection_window can be filled progressively; if allow_partial=true the server may return early with partial window and a continuation_token to resume remaining items.
backwards compatibility: v1 callers (top_k) remain supported for 3 releases; mismatch behavior will return a deprecation header and mapping rules (top_k -> limit, offset=0).

performance: server will prioritize returning the first 'limit' client-visible items using early-stopping heuristics; continuation resumes at stored cursor to avoid re-running full rank across all candidates.
security: continuation token is HMAC-signed to prevent tampering; token expiry defaults to 15 minutes but is configurable per-project policy.
pagination tradeoff: continuation tokens avoid re-scoring entire candidate sets but can pin expensive state in memory; autosweeper will garbage collect tokens after expiry to bound memory growth.
acceptance_criteria: API accepts selection_window (offset, limit, allow_partial) and returns deterministic ordering for repeated requests with same model+seed.
Responses include normalized_score, raw_score, and provenance per item; fields match RFC-like doc and JSON schema in design doc link.
Continuation token roundtrip: server accepts token produced by prior response and returns the next slice; tokens are opaque and validated by server HMAC.
Latency tests: P95 latency for common 50-item window under standard load does not regress more than 15% vs current top_k baseline.
Scale tests: continuation mechanism reduces repeated compute for multi-page reads in benchmark harness by at least 35% for large candidate pools (>=10k).
Client library updates (JS + Python) implement helper wrappers to use selection_window and continuation transparently; integration tests pass.
rollout_plan: Feature-flag v2 rerank endpoint controlled by header X-Rerank-API-Version: v2 (default v1) for 4 weeks in staging.
Canary: enable v2 for 5% of hosted-traffic with detailed tracing and compare per-request compute vs baseline for 72h.
Gradual ramp to 25% then 100% after monitoring thresholds (CPU, GPU cycles, token cost) are stable.
Deprecate v1: announce 3 months before turning off; keep emulation layer for legacy clients for additional 3 months if needed.
risks_mitigations: Risk: Clients may rely on implicit 'top_k' semantics and be surprised by offset semantics. Mitigation: strong docs, deprecation header, and client lib shim that maps top_k to selection_window.
Risk: Continuation tokens pin server state and increase memory. Mitigation: signed opaque cursor with compact representation + TTL + autosweeper and quota per-tenant.
Risk: Partial windows cause inconsistent UX (flashing lists). Mitigation: default allow_partial=false for UI-facing endpoints; set allow_partial=true for batch/throughput-optimized callers.
Risk: Score normalization differences across model variants. Mitigation: include model_version in response and require normalization algorithm to be in model metadata.
test_plan: Unit tests for token encoding/decoding, HMAC verification, and expiration corner cases.
Determinism tests: replay same request (model+seed) 1k times across different nodes; assert identical ordering and scores.
Load test: simulate multi-page UI reads with 10k candidate sets; measure CPU/GPU token work saved by continuation vs re-run.
Contract tests: client libraries assert schema and fallback behavior when server returns partial window + continuation.
E2E: integrate with console trace dashboards to ensure cost breakdowns per-request correctly attribute resumed work.
